section: ## Section 8 — Loss Offset and Carry-Forward / ### 8.3 Anti-Abuse Rule (Norma Antirecompra) — Article 33.5.f LIRPF
wording: - **Re-acquisition rule (2 months)** — Spain has a re-acquisition rule similar to (but distinct from) the US wash sale rule: If you sell a crypto asset at a loss and reacquire the same asset (homogeneous) within 2 months (before or after the sale), the loss is suspended — it cannot be recognised until the replacement asset is itself disposed of outside the 2-month window. For assets traded on a regulated market, the period extends to 1 year (before or after). Most crypto is NOT on a regulated market, so the 2-month rule applies. The suspended loss is not lost — it is added to the cost basis of the replacement asset.  _(Article 33.5.f Ley 35/2006 LIRPF; DGT consulta V1604-18)_

section: ## The base / ### 2. Compute sales and swaps separately
wording: For an ordinary different-coin swap, write `M = max(market value given, market value received)` **before** the separately evidenced transaction expenses. Record qualifying expense attributable to the outgoing disposal as `Eout`, and qualifying expense attributable to acquisition of the incoming coins as `Ein`. An outgoing expense is not also subtracted from the incoming basis: doing so would reverse its deduction on the later sale. The [AEAT swap explanation and LIRPF35/37](https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es/Sede/ayuda/manuales-videos-folletos/manuales-practicos/irpf-2025/c11-ganancias-perdidas-patrimoniales/monedas-virtuales/compra-venta-monedas-virtuales-tributacion-inversor.html) distinguish the swap valuation carried to the received asset from the directly attributable costs in each acquisition/disposal value.

wording: **One mixed fee, one supported allocation:** first establish that the taxpayer bore the charge and that its actual service is inherent in the acquisition/disposal. A missing service/price breakdown is an evidence gap; the label “gas”, “funding”, “withdrawal” or “network fee” alone establishes neither the qualifying expense nor its allocation. section: ## Two worked examples that recompute / ### 2. Cross-exchange FIFO, unequal swap values and limited loss offset
wording: Assume the same minimum/no-credit conditions. The investor bought 10 ETH for total 12,000 at exchange A, then 5 ETH for 10,000 at exchange B. In 2026 they swap **12 ETH**, worth 45,600, for BTC worth 44,000; no fees. Global FIFO uses the first 10 ETH plus two from the second lot: cost **16,000**. The greater-market-value rule makes transfer value **45,600**, giving gain **29,600** and received-BTC basis **45,600**; remaining three ETH retain cost **6,000**. Separately evidenced admissible disposal losses of 33,000 make the disposal basket **−3,400**. Qualifying V1766-22 staking income of 10,000 is in the investment-income basket. Only 2,500 of loss crosses to that basket, leaving taxable savings **7,500**, tax **1,455**, and **900** eligible loss carried forward. No reacquisition issue or other loss restriction is assumed.
